title: 2685. Count the Number of Complete Components

examples.explanation: From the picture above, one can see that all of the components of this graph are complete.

The component containing vertices 0, 1, and 2 is complete since there is an edge between every pair of two vertices. On the other hand, the component containing vertices 3, 4, and 5 is not complete since there is no edge between vertices 4 and 5. Thus, the number of complete components in this graph is 1.

hints: Find the connected components of an undirected graph using depth-first search (DFS) or breadth-first search (BFS).
For each connected component, count the number of nodes and edges in the component.
A connected component is complete if and only if the number of edges in the component is equal to m*(m-1)/2, where m is the number of nodes in the component.
